description: Team for NASA Space Apps Challenge Calgary 2026.
summary:
EarthBeat is an hex globe that makes NISAR radar easy to see and use. Real terrain, land cover, and places sit under NASA–ISRO SAR scenes. You scrub dates, watch water rise and drain, and read change as maps and plain numbers instead of grey static.

It answers the Dancing with the SARs challenge: track surface change worldwide with NISAR. Our lead story is the Sylhet haor wetlands in Bangladesh, about 1,400 km² of monsoon floodwater draining from mid-September to late October 2026. We also show floods, forests and fires, crops, soil moisture, ice, and earthquake motion. Polarisation choices, optical and land-cover context, and a Learn SAR path cover the drivers, channels, and future uses the brief asks for.

Earth’s surface keeps changing under cloud and at night, when optical satellites fail. Radar still sees. Communities, educators, and managers need one clear picture of where water, farms, forests, and ground are moving. EarthBeat makes that dance easy to see, understand, and share.
details:
What / how: EarthBeat is a 3D hex globe that drapes real NISAR radar on terrain. You pick floods, plants, soil, ice, or earthquakes, pick a place, Show radar, scrub dates. Lead story: Sylhet haors, about 1,400 km² of monsoon water draining Sep–Oct 2026. Water tab = blue open water + orange water that left; also Change, Photo, C-band. Radar sees through cloud. Tile server caches everything so the browser never hits APIs with secrets.

Benefits / impact: Cloud-proof flood/crop views, km² numbers, one UI for many change types, Learn SAR teaching, open MIT. Goal: anyone can watch a NISAR season without a radar degree.

Stack: TypeScript, Vite, Node tile server, Three.js, MediaPipe hands, geotiff; NISAR via ASF, NASA GIBS/POWER/FIRMS, Sentinel-1, OSM, terrain tiles, Open-Meteo, etc. Laptop + optional webcam.

Creative / team: Living hex Earth, cloud-then-radar demo, hand control, story cards. Shared Sylhet focus, GitHub issue #1 claims, humans + agents.
dataRefs: NISAR L2 GCOV, GUNW and GOFF data (ASF DAAC)

projectRefs: Sentinel-1 GRD radar (ESA Copernicus, via ASF)
